question: Which product is formed when sodium bicarbonate is heated strongly?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sodium Carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **sodium bicarbonate** (NaHCO₃) is heated strongly, it decomposes to form **sodium carbonate** (Na₂CO₃), water (H₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• The chemical equation for this decomposition reaction is:

 2 NaHCO₃ (s) → Na₂CO₃ (s) + H₂O (g) + CO₂ (g).
 
• This process is commonly used in the production of **soda ash** (sodium carbonate).
 
• **Sodium carbonate** is an important industrial chemical used in the manufacture of glass, paper, detergents, and many other products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide**__

 __
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** (NaOH), also known as **caustic soda** or **lye**, is a highly caustic metallic base and alkali.
 
• It is used in many industrial applications, including the manufacture of paper, textiles, and detergents.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Peroxide**__
 __
 
• **Sodium peroxide** (Na₂O₂) is a strong oxidizing agent used in chemical synthesis and as a bleaching agent.
 
• It reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Monoxide**__
 
 
• **Sodium monoxide** (Na₂O) is a chemical compound consisting of sodium and oxygen.
 
• It is less commonly encountered and used compared to sodium carbonate and sodium hydroxide.
